why: I checked every command against the repo. The named files all exist (index.js, README.md, test/strutil.test.js, package.json with a `test` script). `npm test` and the Check 1, 2 and 4 commands look runnable. Check 3 breaks. Its JavaScript sits inside a double-quoted shell string, and bash turns `\\` into `\`. So node receives `'^#{1,6}\s+\x60?'+f+'\b'` as plain JS string literals. There `\s` becomes just `s` and `\b` becomes a backspace character. The regex is then `^#{1,6}s+`?name<BS>`, which matches no README heading. The command runs, but it always reports every export as missing. A correct README would get a false FAIL, so the quoting doesn't produce the command the brief intends. Because the shell and JS escaping in Check 3 is wrong, the criterion does not hold for the whole output.
